answer: A haven wildlife refuge buys trellis designs that keep raven nests safe. Before bidding, each agent locks a 30-day warranty bond tied to the job ID. The market hashes design files and groups near-duplicates, paying only one accepted design per group after an independent installer and a random inspector sign off. Fifty aliases copying one plan gain one fee; fifty separate bids freeze fifty bonds and require distinct workable designs, raising capital and labor costs. Inspectors may collude or overlook delayed damage, so the bond stays disputable and buyers can appeal with dated photos.
